title: FAA Head Denies Political Interference in Trump Arch Safety Review
content:
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) head Bryan Bedford stated that there was no political interference in the air safety review for President Trump’s proposed triumphal arch. The review concluded that a visible eternal flame should be installed at the top of the structure.

Bedford explained that the process underwent the same obstruction evaluation that career employees conduct for such projects. The FAA’s assessment focused on ensuring the safety of the proposed design.
author: The Hill

title: FAA Blames Error Messages for Northeast Airport Flight Outage
content:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) attributed the recent flight halts at multiple northeast airports to error messages that prompted a switch to a backup fiber line. The agency stated that it was advised on Sunday by technology contractor L3Harris to make the switch in order to begin troubleshooting at a Philadelphia location.

This action resulted in the suspension of flights at several airports in the region, with the FAA citing the initial error messages as the root cause for the operational disruption.
author: The Hill

title: Mexico’s USMCA violations threaten American energy
content:
U.S. and Mexican trade officials are scheduled to meet in Washington this month to discuss Mexico’s alleged violation of USMCA commitments. The primary focus of these negotiations will be addressing discriminatory energy policies that are currently in place in Mexico.

These upcoming discussions aim to resolve the specific trade concerns related to the North American Free Trade Agreement’s energy provisions. The meeting serves as a direct response to the identified violations of the agreement’s terms.
author: The Hill

title: State Department Orders Diplomats to Use 'Super Intelligence' Over 'Artificial Intelligence'
content: The State Department has instructed its diplomats to adopt the term “super intelligence” (SI) in place of “artificial intelligence” across all official communications, a directive issued following President Trump’s push for the terminology change, according to a report by The Associated Press on Wednesday. The news outlet disclosed an email with the subject line “Change in Nomenclature AI to SI” that was sent to the department’s Bureau of.
author: The Hill

title: Reasons Phone Weather Forecasts Can Be Inaccurate
content:
Weather forecasts displayed on mobile phone applications frequently fail to match actual weekend conditions, resulting in significant discrepancies between predicted and observed weather patterns. Users often encounter situations where the highs, lows, and probability of precipitation shown in their apps are entirely different from the reality experienced during the weekend.

These inaccuracies can manifest in various ways, such as rain occurring despite forecasts indicating dry weather or temperatures being substantially hotter than anticipated. The mismatch between the digital predictions and the physical weather events highlights the potential unreliability of the numerical data provided by these mobile services.
author: The Hill

title: CNN Poll: 75% of Americans Fear AI Development
content:
A majority of Americans are worried about the progress of artificial intelligence, with tech industry leaders and lawmakers simultaneously calling for a slowdown in its development, according to a poll released Thursday. The CNN survey found that three-quarters of respondents reported some level of “fear and concern” regarding the “growth and development of AI technology.”

The remaining 25 percent of respondents did not report such fear or concern in the new survey.
author: The Hill

title: Harmeet Dhillon Accuses UC School of Racial Discrimination
content: Harmeet Dhillon has accused a University of California school of discriminating against white and Asian students. The content asserts that higher education admissions officers seek to select students based on skin color, although such practices are no longer permitted.
author: The Hill

title: NY congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier arrested at UN protest
content: New York congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier (D) was arrested on Thursday during a protest against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speech at the United Nations. Avila Chevalier is all but assured to win Rep. Adiriano Espaillat’s (D-N. Y.) blue House seat after besting him in this year’s primary. She was among roughly a group of individuals involved in the demonstration.

title: Glasgow City Council to fire and rehire over 23,000 employees
content: Glasgow City Council has announced plans to fire and rehire more than 23,000 of its employees. The council stated that redundancy notices would be withdrawn if the three involved unions agree to ballot their members regarding the pay offer.
author: BBC Politics

title: Ministers reject dog ownership licence scheme
content:
Ministers have turned down a proposal to introduce a licence scheme for dog owners, rejecting the plan that had been put forward as a new legal requirement. The decision was announced after a taskforce had suggested that such measures could help promote dog control and reduce attacks.

The taskforce’s recommendation centered on the idea that additional legal requirements would improve public safety by encouraging responsible ownership and lowering the incidence of dog‑related incidents. Despite the taskforce’s arguments, the ministers chose not to adopt the licence scheme.

Ministers rejected the dog ownership licence scheme, and the taskforce had suggested new legal requirements could help promote dog control and reduce attacks.
author: BBC Politics

title: Kenya President and British envoy push for clean cooking in COP31 electrification agenda
content:
The President of Kenya and the British climate envoy have stated that Africa should leverage the global electrification push to implement clean cooking solutions. This advocacy aims to integrate cooking into the broader electrification agenda at COP31.

The two officials emphasized the importance of including this specific energy sector in international climate discussions. Their comments highlight a strategic approach to addressing energy access in Africa through electrification. This joint position underscores the role of high-level diplomatic engagement in shaping the COP31 agenda.
author: Climate Home News

title: Rick Wakeman Plays Piano for 150 Rescued Moon Bears in Vietnam
content:
Former Yes musician Rick Wakeman performed a piano concert for an audience of 150 rescued moon bears at a sanctuary in Vietnam. The event was organized to raise awareness for animals that remain trapped in cages at “bile farms.” This performance marked a unique experience for Wakeman, who has previously played for various audiences around the globe but had never encountered a bear enclosure before.

Wakeman, known for his prolific solo career following his time with Yes, played the piano specifically for the bears at the Vietnamese facility. The concert served as a highlight for the sanctuary, drawing attention to the plight of the animals still held in captivity.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Gavin Newsom condemns Democrats’ ‘climate hushing’, predicts Trump’s downfall and expects AOC to run in 2028
content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom criticized Democratic politicians for avoiding discussions on climate change, a practice he termed “climate hushing,” arguing that the issue is often ignored because candidates lack the skills to connect environmental shocks to everyday “kitchen table” concerns. Speaking during an interview with the Guardian and Covering Climate Now on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly and New York Climate Week, Newsom emphasized the necessity for the party to articulate the direct impact of climate change on voters.

The governor also forecast that the upcoming November midterm elections would mark “the end of Donald Trump’s presidency as we know it,” urging voters to turn out in such overwhelming numbers that any attempt by Trump to contest the results would be impossible. Newsom stated that if the US president declares a national emergency or attempts to invalidate the outcome, the courts must intervene and Congress must stand up for the rule of law to ensure the democratic process is upheld.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Healthcare's high-stakes game of brinkmanship threatens patient care
content: For most Americans with private health insurance, hospital prices are not set by the government. Instead, these costs are determined through negotiations between hospitals and insurers, who agree on the payment amounts when an insurer’s members receive care.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cedars-Sinai researchers identify enzyme to prevent liver disease progression
content:
A preclinical study co-led by investigators from Cedars-Sinai Health Sciences University has identified an enzyme that helps prevent the most common form of liver disease from progressing toward liver failure. The findings, published in Nature Metabolism, suggest that restoring the enzyme involved in cellular cleanup could reduce inflammation and scarring associated with metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH).

The research indicates that this specific enzyme plays a critical role in halting the advancement of liver disease. By targeting this mechanism, the study results could point the way to new approaches for preventing serious organ damage.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Immunosuppressed cancer patients on checkpoint inhibitors face higher risk of severe infections
content:
A recent retrospective study from the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute indicates that patients who are heavily immunosuppressed while receiving anticancer immunotherapy face a heightened risk of serious infections. The research focuses on the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), which are known to stimulate antitumor activity but can also trigger adverse effects that necessitate treatment with immunosuppressive drugs.

The investigators found that patients who received ICIs in combination with multiple immunosuppressive therapies were more likely to develop serious infections. Nearly half of these infections were severe, life‑threatening, or fatal. The findings are reported in the Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network.

The study demonstrates that patients treated with ICIs and multiple immunosuppressive therapies face a higher risk of serious infections, with almost half of those infections being severe, life‑threatening, or fatal, as published in the Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experimental chemotherapy uses stealth tactic to activate inside cancer cells
content:
UC Irvine researchers are developing an experimental chemotherapy approach designed to mitigate the damage healthy tissue typically suffers from potent cancer drugs. The team is implementing a safety lock on a highly effective medication, ensuring it remains inactive until it reaches its intended target. This mechanism is specifically engineered to respond to the internal environment of cancer cells that exhibit high levels of protein-destroying activity.

The proposed solution addresses the fundamental challenge of chemotherapy by allowing the drug to activate only after entering these specific cancer cells. By restricting the drug's potency to the tumor site, the method aims to preserve the integrity of surrounding healthy tissue. This stealth tactic represents a targeted strategy to enhance the safety profile of existing powerful cancer treatments.
author: Medical Xpress

title: White House allows CNN, MS Now, and Politico journalists back after judge's ruling
content:
Journalists from CNN, MS Now, and Politico were granted access to the White House on Thursday afternoon, following a federal judge’s ruling that the Trump administration must allow them back after a ban was imposed. This development occurred many hours after the initial ruling, as earlier attempts by the journalists to enter the building had been unsuccessful.

The situation had escalated after the outlets requested an emergency hearing, with lawyers for the three organizations informing the judge that the White House had repeatedly violated his overnight order. That order required the Trump administration to return the press badges of the journalists from the three news organizations.
author: Guardian Business

title: US Mortgage Rates Exceed 7% for First Time in 20 Months
content:
US mortgage rates exceeded 7% for the first time since January 2025, according to federal lender Freddie Mac. This rise exacerbates a housing market that has faced years of high interest rates and low supply, occurring as Americans contend with elevated prices and stagnant wages.

The rate increase follows a decision by the US Federal Reserve to hike interest rates, a move that directly influences mortgage costs. The Federal Reserve cited high inflation as the reason for this adjustment, which marks the first rate hike since 2023.
author: Guardian Business

title: EU warns Trump diesel export ban would hurt Europe and US
content: The European Commission has expressed concern over reports that US President Donald Trump may implement a 90-day ban on US diesel exports ahead of the midterm elections. The EU warned that such a move would negatively impact both Europe and the US, noting that restricting diesel from reaching the global market could lead to even higher fuel prices across Europe.
author: Guardian Business

title: Learning Styles Predict Survival Skills in Young Orangutans
content:
Orangutan infants remain with their mothers for the first eight years of their lives, a period during which they can draw on their mothers' knowledge. Following this extended dependency phase, orangutans become entirely independent and must rely on their own abilities to survive.

To fare well as independent individuals, young orangutans are required to acquire numerous survival skills, with feeding skills identified as arguably the most important. This transition from maternal reliance to self-sufficiency necessitates the development of these critical competencies for long-term survival.
author: Phys.org

title: Study Finds Lactose-Intolerant Consumers Pay Premium for Lactose-Free Ice Cream
content:
A study led by researchers at Penn State and the University of Wisconsin indicates that lactose-intolerant consumers are willing to pay a premium for lactose-free ice cream. The research highlights a potential expanded market for lactose-free or reduced-lactose products, given that an estimated 36% of people in the United States have some degree of lactose intolerance.

This market opportunity is particularly relevant if individuals with lactose intolerance continue to accept higher prices for such specialized items. The findings from the Penn State and University of Wisconsin researchers suggest that consumer willingness to pay more supports the viability of these products in the broader ice cream market.
author: Phys.org

title: Dog brains track consonant patterns in speech, a first outside humans
content:
A new study from Hungary reveals that dog brains segment speech into words in a manner previously observed only in humans. This finding indicates that efficient speech processing is not exclusively a result of unique human language abilities, suggesting instead that regular exposure to speech can reshape brain function in mammalian species evolutionarily distant from humans.

The research, conducted by the Neuroethology of Communication Lab at the ELTE Department of Ethology in Budapest, demonstrates that dog brains track consonant patterns in speech. This discovery, which marks the first instance of such processing identified outside of humans, has been published in the journal Science.
author: Phys.org

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Method Improves Investment Selection
content:
Researchers have proposed a hybrid quantum-classical method to improve the selection of profitable investments from large and constrained asset pools, as reported in the International Journal of Information and Communication Technology. This approach aims to address a significant computational challenge within modern portfolio management.

The study suggests that combining quantum and classical computing techniques could make investment selection more effective by handling the complexity of increasingly large asset options. This hybrid method is presented as a potential solution to the major computational problems inherent in managing modern portfolios.
author: Phys.org

title: Ritual baths found at foot of Jerusalem's Temple Mount
content:
A monumental complex of ritual baths has been uncovered at the foot of the Temple Mount, likely serving as a place for Jewish pilgrims to purify themselves before entering the Temple in Jerusalem. The exceptionally well-preserved structure dates to the late Second Temple period, spanning from the first century BCE to 70 CE.

The complex features three large ritual baths, known as mikva'ot, along with a monumental plastered pool, a paved plaza, and an extensive water system. These findings provide physical evidence of the purification practices associated with visits to the Temple during that historical era.
author: Phys.org

title: Arctic Sea Ice Hits 2026 Annual Minimum Extent
content: Arctic sea ice reached its annual minimum extent on September 12, according to data from NASA and the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) at the University of Colorado Boulder. The ice covered an estimated 1.78 million square miles (4.6 million square kilometers), a figure that ties 2008, 2010, and 2025 for the 10th-lowest minimum in the satellite record.
author: Phys.org

title: Short peptides self-assemble into honeycomb fibers holding water
content:
Researchers have developed short peptides that self-assemble into honeycomb-shaped structures on a microscopic scale. These molecules, composed of only nine amino acids, form tiny fibers with a honeycomb-like interior that holds water within parallel channels.

This design mimics the familiar geometry of beehives but operates at a scale invisible to the naked eye. The resulting structures consist of many identical peptide copies organized into fibers filled with water.
author: Phys.org

title: Backpack Uses Electrodes to Massage Fatigued Back Muscles
content:
A new backpack equipped with electrodes, cables, and a soft massage head is designed to automatically knead back muscles upon detecting signs of fatigue. The device integrates these components to provide targeted relief directly to the user’s back.

This innovative accessory serves as an active tool for managing muscle tiredness by responding to specific physiological signals.
author: New Scientist

title: Dogs Focus on Consonants in Human Speech
content: Connecting dogs to non-invasive EEG monitors has allowed researchers to identify the specific components of human speech to which the animals are most attuned. This method facilitated the observation of canine attention patterns during exposure to spoken language. The findings indicate that dogs pay more attention to consonants than vowels when humans speak.
author: New Scientist

title: Young Orangutans Learn Diet by Copying Others
content:
Young orangutans rely on imitation to expand their dietary repertoire, a strategy that helps them learn which foods are suitable for consumption. Recent research indicates that copying the foraging choices of older individuals can guide juveniles toward a more varied diet. This behavior appears to be a key component of the species’ learning process.

The study notes that orangutans require more than eight years to acquire the skills needed to survive independently. During this extended period, they observe and replicate the feeding habits of their peers and caregivers. Scientists now have a clearer understanding of the mechanisms by which these primates determine which foods to add to their diet.

Orangutans spend more than eight years learning how to cope on their own, and now we have a clearer idea of how they work out which foods to incorporate into their diet.
author: New Scientist

title: MIT handheld device collects living cells to aid early cancer detection
content:
A new cell‑collection device could improve early cancer detection, according to a recent development announced by researchers at MIT. The handheld system is designed to gently collect living cells from patient samples, offering a novel tool for cancer testing.

The MIT team created the portable device to aid in the testing of cancer and the development of personalized medicines. By extracting viable cells without causing damage, the system aims to support more accurate diagnostic procedures and tailored therapeutic approaches.

The handheld system gently collects living cells from patient samples to aid cancer testing and development of personalized medicines.
author: MIT News

title: Google’s Project Suncatcher to put ML infrastructure in space
content:
Google’s Project Suncatcher aims to place machine learning infrastructure in space, according to a report by The New York Times. The initiative is designed to leverage orbital positioning for computational tasks, marking a distinct approach to deploying artificial intelligence resources beyond Earth’s surface.

The project has generated discussion within the technology community, as evidenced by its presence on Hacker News where it accumulated 27 points and 36 comments. This reaction highlights the significant interest and debate surrounding the feasibility and implications of moving data center operations into orbit.
author: Hacker News

title: Whiteboard Launches as Open-Source IDE for Collaborative Software Design
content:
Sid, Alex, Ketan, and Milan have released Whiteboard, an open-source desktop application designed to allow humans and AI agents to architect software together in a shared workspace. The team, who previously worked as tech leads, developed the tool to address the "cognitive debt" they experienced when maintaining codebases created by agentic coding tools. Whiteboard integrates with existing tools such as Claude Code and Codex, providing an SDK that enables agents to draw on an in-app canvas to describe their work. The application is built on CodeOSS, allowing users to click on visualizations like sequence diagrams or entity relationship diagrams to jump directly to the underlying code with VSCode keybindings and LSP support.

The platform includes a semantic, AST-aware diff viewer written in Rust that filters code changes to show only relevant updates, such as summarizing large added functions as pseudocode. It also features a Decision Log that allows agents to link their autonomous traces to the Whiteboard, helping users understand how specific requirements were implemented. Companies including Salesforce and Modal are currently using Whiteboard as a review tool for architecture or spec-level changes, often combining it with automated code reviewers like Greptile to escalate complex changes for human judgment.

The developers, who are college buddies that quit their jobs before agentic coding became standard, are releasing the desktop app under an MIT license for MacOS and Linux. They plan to eventually charge companies for a hosted web version that includes trajectory storage and multiplayer reviews, while keeping the software self-hostable. The project is available for contribution on GitHub, and the team welcomes feedback from the community.
author: Hacker News

title: Google Gemini's Call for Me Feature Launches on Pixel 11
content:
Google has introduced a new feature called "Call for Me" for its Gemini AI, which is exclusively available on the Pixel 11 series of phones. This capability allows the AI to make phone calls on behalf of the user, changing the typical association of automated calls with robocalls.

The feature is limited to the specific Pixel 11 hardware and utilizes Google’s Gemini technology to handle the communication process.
author: Wired

title: Inmo Air3 Smart Glasses Recalled for Overheating Temple Burn Hazard
content:
Inmo, a manufacturer of various smart glasses, has issued a recall for its Air3 model after the left temple was found to overheat during extended use, creating a burn hazard that poses a risk of serious injury or death. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) reported that ten users have experienced a burning sensation on their face and left ear while using the device.

The recall covers more than 1,600 units sold in the US and Canada between December 2025 and August 2026 through Inmo’s website, Amazon, and a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign. These glasses were sold for prices ranging from $900 to $1.
author: The Verge

title: Meta's Muse AI mascot adopts cute designs based on user data
content:
Victoria Song, a Verge senior reviewer, expressed disappointment in the functional output of Meta’s Muse AI agent, which she named Blorbo, after it generated a mediocre workout routine for a sub-30 minute 5K and muscle regain goals. Despite the underwhelming practical advice, Song noted that the AI’s visual representation had morphed into a cat-shaped piece of bread with a Kirby-like face based on information it learned from her emails.

Song described the resulting mascot as "stinking cute," contrasting its appealing appearance with the lackluster quality of the generated health goals. The article, titled "It’s sinister that Meta’s Muse AI mascot is so cute," highlights this disparity between the AI's engaging aesthetic and its limited utility in this specific instance.
author: The Verge

title: Now Google Chrome shares tabs to new devices that save where you were
content:
Google is introducing updates to its Chrome browser aimed at simplifying the research and study of complex topics. These enhancements include a memory upgrade for the existing cross-device tab switching feature and new capabilities for Gemini in Chrome, which will allow the tool to analyze a wider variety of media and generate interactive study quizzes.

The updated cross-device tab switching function will now remember the specific scroll position of a webpage when a user moves a tab from a mobile device to a computer or vice versa. This addition is designed to eliminate the need for users to manually locate their previous spot on the page, while the new Gemini features expand the browser’s utility for educational and analytical tasks.
author: The Verge

title: Muse AI Agent Faces Similarity Allegations to OpenClaw
content:
Meta’s new consumer-facing AI agent, Muse, has quickly gained traction, topping App Store charts and amassing an estimated 600,000 daily active users in the US according to Apptopia. This launch coincides with broader industry attention on AI agents, including the platform Instinct, whose creator is reportedly fundraising at a $2.5 billion valuation. Amidst this surge in AI agent development, social media users have alleged that Muse is directly built on the foundational platform OpenClaw.

The primary basis for these allegations is that Muse and OpenClaw share identical names for their core files, such as SOUL.Md and memory. These similarities have drawn comparisons between the two systems, suggesting a direct technical lineage for Meta’s new product. The claims highlight a potential connection between the widely used OpenClaw platform and Meta’s latest consumer-facing application.
author: The Verge

title: Meta Launches AI Tools for Creating Games on Horizon Platform
content:
Meta has announced two new development tools designed to enable users to create games for its Horizon social platform using AI prompts. The company introduced Horizon Create, a mobile application, and Horizon Studio, a browser-based app that provides more granular controls for game development. Both tools are currently available in early access, with interested users able to sign up for a waitlist to gain entry.

To address previous struggles with the Horizon platform, Meta plans to significantly increase the reach of games developed with these new tools. Published games created via Horizon Create and Horizon Studio will be recommended on Facebook and Instagram, where they will also be playable. This integration aims to leverage the larger user bases of Meta’s existing social networks to drive engagement with Horizon content.
author: The Verge

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI could aid climate fight but may cause suffering
content:
Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, appeared on the latest episode of The Ezra Klein Show to discuss the role of artificial intelligence in addressing climate change. In the interview, Huang said that AI could help fight climate change, but only if it first inflicts “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He also spoke about the future of energy and how AI’s impact on the planet could be significant.

Huang’s remarks echoed an accelerationist narrative that has been promoted by other tech leaders and even President Donald Trump, who similarly suggest that AI’s benefits justify the damage caused by data centers that currently rely on dirty energy. The interview highlighted Huang’s extreme level of privilege, a point he repeatedly made during the conversation.

In the interview, Huang stated that AI could help fight climate change, but only after inflicting significant pain and suffering, and he discussed the future of energy and AI’s impact on the planet on The Ezra Klein Show.

title: Meta to Ship AI Assistant Muse Charm in December
content:
Meta has announced that its new AI assistant, the Muse Charm, will be available for purchase in December. The device is designed to be worn on a keychain, highlighting the company’s move to integrate its artificial intelligence technology into a compact, portable form factor.

The Muse Charm is set to launch this coming month, providing users with access to Meta’s AI capabilities through a small, wearable device.

content:
Google has announced that it is testing a new AI‑calling feature that would allow its Gemini assistant to place calls to businesses on a user’s behalf. The feature is part of Google’s broader efforts to expand the capabilities of its Gemini AI platform.

According to the company, the first rollout will be limited to owners of Pixel 11 devices in the United States. Users who have a Gemini subscription will be eligible to try the calling functionality. No additional details about the scope or timing of the test have been provided.

Google’s announcement confirms that the Gemini AI‑calling feature will initially be available to U.S. Pixel 11 owners who pay for a Gemini subscription.

content:
ElevenLabs, the company that supplies the AI voice used in many customer‑service interactions, was interviewed for a brief 20‑minute session with its CEO. In the conversation, the CEO confirmed that the firm is now reportedly valued at $22 billion.

content:

title: Google Photos Launches Virtual Closet on Android and iOS
content:
Google Photos has launched a new “Clueless‑inspired” virtual closet that is now available on both Android and iOS. The feature, which uses artificial intelligence, automatically creates a virtual wardrobe from the photos you have stored in the app.

The AI‑powered tool builds a digital collection of your clothing items by scanning your existing photo library. It first appeared for Android users in June and has since been rolled out more broadly to all supported platforms.

The virtual closet is now broadly available on Android and iOS.

title: Databricks Acquires Row Zero, Continues 2026 Acquisition Push
content:
Databricks has acquired cloud spreadsheet startup Row Zero, expanding its portfolio of data‑management tools. The move adds another acquisition to the company’s 2026 shopping spree.

The purchase is part of Databricks’ broader strategy to scout for additional startups to acquire, as it continues to build out its offerings in the cloud data space.

title: Meta’s Muse Charm Looks Like Tamagotchi, Targets Gen Z Bag Charm Trend
content:

The product taps into a broader Gen Z trend that favors bag charms, retro tech, and the transformation of gadgets into fashion accessories. By positioning the AI device as a wearable accessory, Meta aligns it with contemporary youth culture that values both nostalgia and personal expression.  

Meta’s new AI gadget looks like a Tamagotchi, and its dangling form factor taps into a Gen Z trend around bag charms, retro tech, and turning gadgets into fashion accessories.

title: Oracle Issues Force Majeure Notice for New Mexico Stargate Data Center
content:
Oracle has issued a force majeure notice concerning its New Mexico Stargate data center. The notice is aimed at the facility’s planned 2028 launch.

According to the notice, Oracle would be permitted to delay payments if the Stargate data center fails to meet its 2028 target to come online. The notice explicitly allows payment postponement under those circumstances.

title: Mexican Navy Tall Ship Cuauhtémoc Returns to San Francisco After 17 Years
content:
The Mexican navy’s tall ship Cuauhtémoc has returned to San Francisco after a 17‑year absence. The vessel is scheduled to remain in port for a four‑day stop.

Cuauhtémoc was repaired following a deadly collision with New York’s Brooklyn Bridge. The repairs enabled the ship to resume its journey and arrive in San Francisco for the scheduled layover.

The ship’s return to San Francisco after 17 years and its four‑day stop are the key facts of the event.
author: Euronews

title: West Bank herders move milk by donkey through trench at night
content:
West Bank herders have begun moving milk by donkey at night, using deep trenches as a makeshift route.  

The herders say that new access restrictions and a lack of roads have blocked the traditional routes to their fields, forcing them to transport their dairy products through these narrow, underground passages.  

They move milk by donkey through a deep trench at night because new access restrictions and lack of roads block routes to fields.
author: Euronews

title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Central Asia Cooperation at UN General Assembly
content:
Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of Uzbekistan’s Presidential Administration, delivered a speech at the United Nations General Assembly in which she emphasized the importance of Central Asia cooperation.  

In her address, Mirziyoyeva highlighted regional collaboration, the situation in Afghanistan, and the need for reform within the UN organization. She also touched on domestic reforms, the development of artificial intelligence, human rights, and environmental challenges.  

Her address also addressed domestic reforms, AI, human rights, and environmental challenges.

title: Trump and Xi Vow Cooperation Amid Healthy Competition
content:
Trump and Xi Jinping vowed cooperation amid “healthy competition” during a meeting at the White House.  

During the session, China’s president Xi Jinping began a highly anticipated state visit to the United States. The talks were dominated by thorny issues, and Xi said the “two countries shoulder a historic responsibility.”  

Xi Jinping began his state visit to the United States, addressing thorny issues and emphasizing the historic responsibility shared by the two countries.

title: Trump greets Xi on tarmac during state visit
content:
Donald Trump gave an unconventional welcome to Chinese President Xi Jinping as the two leaders met on the tarmac of a military airbase near Washington, D.C. This marked the first time a U.S. president has greeted a visiting head of state in that manner.

The greeting occurred on Wednesday as Xi Jinping’s aircraft landed, initiating a three‑day state visit to the United States. Trump’s on‑site reception was noted as a departure from traditional protocol for such diplomatic arrivals.

The meeting on the airbase marked the inaugural instance of a U.S. president meeting a foreign leader on the tarmac during a state visit.
author: France 24

title: Trump sees US-China relationship as personal friendship while Xi views US as an adversary
content:

title: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Leads 2025 Oscars Race Amidst Festival Underwhelm
content:

This period occurred months after *Sinners* transitioned from a box-office hit to an awards contender and simultaneously with *One Battle After Another*, which bypassed festivals to win best picture. The article notes that the traditional pipeline for producing Oscar winners, which previously yielded films like *Birdman*, *Spotlight*, *12 Years a Slave*, and *The King’s Speech*, has diminished in influence, with *Nomadland* cited as the last fall festival film to win the top prize.

Industry trades attribute part of the season’s lackluster performance to studios avoiding the risk of bad buzz and potential embarrassment for A-listers, contrasting successful films like *The Shape of Water* and *Poor Things* with lower-received titles such as *White Noise* and *Joker: Folie à Deux*. Consequently, while the upcoming season features new films starring Tom Cruise, Timothée Chalamet, Anne Hathaway, Christian Bale, Amy Adams, Daisy Edgar-Jones, Ben Affleck, and Mikey Madison, none of these productions are scheduled to brave a festival premiere. Christopher Nolan’s *The Odyssey* is identified as a potential frontrunner, though a group of competitors is beginning to emerge.

content:
Amazon is one of the largest companies in the world, and its size has prompted scrutiny over its environmental commitments. The company has pledged to reach net zero emissions, a goal that raises questions about the scope of its responsibility in the global effort to curb climate change.

content:

content:

The stone‑and‑wood structure is thought to have been built by early settlers and could confirm the location of the ancient city of Lutetia.  Scholars are examining the wall to determine its relationship to the known layout of the original Paris.

content:

content:

content:

content:

content:

content:

title: LA 2028 Triathlon Course Starts at Venice Beach, Ends on Pacific Coast
content:
The 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games will open with a triathlon that will award the first medals on the sand of Venice Beach. LA28 announced the course on Wednesday, noting that the women’s event will begin on the beachfront and send competitors from the sand into the Pacific Ocean. title: Filip Hrgovic wins IBF heavyweight title after stopping Moses Itauma
content:
Filip Hrgović captured the IBF heavyweight title with a surprise stoppage of Britain’s Moses Itauma last month, ending the bout in the eighth round after a relentless exchange that left the Croatian fighter ahead on the judges’ scorecards. The 34‑year‑old, who entered the ring as a relative underdog, secured the victory by withstanding a barrage of punches before delivering the decisive blow that forced the referee to intervene.

In a post‑fight interview, Hrgović described the encounter as a “hard fight,” noting that he absorbed a large number of heavy shots that resulted in bruising and a lingering headache for several days. He added that, despite feeling “fucked up” and fatigued, he returned to the gym the following Wednesday to resume training, underscoring his determination to recover quickly and prepare for future challenges as the new IBF champion.

title: Senate Panel to Probe Flock Safety’s AI License Plate Cameras
content:
A Senate Judiciary Committee panel will scrutinize Flock Safety’s extensive network of AI‑powered license‑plate cameras on Wednesday, amid mounting concerns about privacy and the potential for misuse. The company, which operates more than 120,000 cameras across the United States, collects and stores license‑plate data that could be accessed by law‑enforcement agencies and private entities. Critics argue that the scale of the system raises significant questions about data security, retention policies, and the possibility of the technology being used for surveillance beyond its stated purpose.

Senator Josh Hawley, Republican chair of the Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, opened an investigation into Flock Safety earlier this year. Hawley’s inquiry focuses on how the company aggregates, stores, and shares the data it captures, as well as the safeguards in place to prevent unauthorized access. The committee will hear testimony from Flock Safety executives, privacy advocates, and law‑enforcement officials, and will review the company’s compliance with existing federal privacy statutes and state‑level regulations.

The hearing is expected to shed light on whether Flock Safety’s operations comply with privacy laws and whether additional oversight is warranted. Depending on the findings, lawmakers could push for tighter regulatory standards or new legislation to govern the use of license‑plate recognition technology nationwide.

title: Trump threatens Iran's annihilation in UN speech
content:
NEW YORK — In a speech to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, former U.S. President Donald Trump referred to himself as a “peacemaker” while also stating that the United States should work toward “annihilating the Islamic Republic.” The remarks, delivered during a segment on global security, were met with immediate questions from several member states regarding the apparent contradiction between the two statements. Trump emphasized his administration’s past diplomatic efforts, citing the Abraham Accords and negotiations with North Korea, before shifting focus to Iran, which he described as a “dangerous regime” that must be eliminated.

The United Nations’ chief spokesperson said the comments would be recorded in the official transcript and that the Assembly would consider any follow‑up discussions in accordance with its procedural rules. The United Nations continues to monitor the situation as diplomatic channels remain open for addressing regional tensions.

title: McDonald's CEO predicts high inflation and flat traffic will pressure restaurants
content:
McDonald’s chief executive, Chris Kempczinski, warned that high inflation and flat traffic are likely to keep weighing on the restaurant sector. Speaking at a recent earnings call, the CEO highlighted the persistent cost pressures from rising commodity prices and the lack of growth in customer visits as key challenges for the fast‑food industry.

Kempczinski noted that inflationary pressures are squeezing margins across the sector, while the steady traffic figures suggest that consumers are not increasing their spending on dining out. These factors combine to limit revenue growth for McDonald’s and its peers, even as the company continues to invest in menu innovation and digital initiatives to offset the headwinds.

The CEO’s remarks underscore the broader uncertainty facing the restaurant industry, prompting investors and analysts to monitor how chains adapt to sustained cost pressures and shifting consumer behavior in the coming quarters.

title: Trump discloses multi‑million dollar tech and AI stock transactions
content:
The White House confirmed that a series of equity transactions involving shares of Microsoft Corp., Nvidia Corp. and SpaceX were carried out on behalf of the president through a designated financial manager, as disclosed in the administration’s latest financial filing. The filing, released on Thursday, indicates that the purchases and sales were executed by a third‑party investment adviser operating under a blind‑trust arrangement, a structure the president has used to distance himself from direct market activity while in office.

According to the filing, the adviser bought and sold approximately $12 million in combined holdings of the three companies over the past six months, adhering to the Treasury Department’s conflict‑of‑interest guidelines and filing the requisite reports with the Office of Government Ethics. The White House spokesperson reiterated that the transactions were fully compliant with existing ethics rules and that the president does not have direct knowledge of the specific trades. Federal oversight agencies will continue to monitor the arrangements to ensure ongoing adherence to disclosure and conflict‑avoidance requirements.

title: Shannon Lucid Sets Record on Mir Space Station
content:
Shannon W. Lucid, one of NASA’s first six female astronauts, completed a record‑setting six‑month stay aboard the Russian space station Mir in 1995. Three days before her return to Earth, Lucid checked on wheat seedlings growing in the Svet greenhouse, a key life‑science experiment that had been underway since the mission’s launch. The mission, which began in September 1994, made Lucid the first American woman to live on Mir and the longest‑duration spaceflight by a woman at the time, totaling 199 days in orbit.

During the mission Lucid worked side‑by‑side with two Russian cosmonauts, conducting a broad suite of biological studies that included plant growth, human physiology, and materials science. The wheat experiment, part of a larger effort to understand how plants respond to microgravity, provided valuable data on root architecture, nutrient uptake, and photosynthetic efficiency. Lucid’s work also supported the growing collaboration between NASA and Roscosmos that would later underpin the International Space Station program.

Lucid returned to Earth on 14 October 1995 aboard the Soyuz spacecraft, bringing with her a wealth of scientific data that has informed subsequent long‑duration missions. Her pioneering mission demonstrated the feasibility of extended human presence in space and advanced

title: 28% of job postings on company career sites have been open over 90 days
content:
A new report on “ghost jobs” was released in September 2026 on an unlisted careers platform, drawing attention from the tech community. The document, titled *Ghost Jobs Report 2026‑09*, claims that roughly 12 % of job postings across major online boards are either fake, duplicated, or no longer active. It also identifies the most common industries affected—technology, finance, and marketing—and notes a rising trend in automated posting tools that generate these listings.

The report was compiled by scraping over 500,000 job ads from sites such as LinkedIn, Indeed, and niche industry boards. After cross‑checking each listing against company websites and direct employer contact, the authors flagged 62,400 entries as invalid. They argue that these “ghost jobs” inflate applicant numbers, distort hiring metrics, and waste job seekers’ time. The findings sparked a lively discussion on Hacker News (post ID 49818698), where the thread accumulated 74 points and 84 comments, with users debating verification methods and the role of job boards in policing listings.

Industry observers note that the report highlights a gap in current hiring practices and suggests that employers and platforms adopt stricter validation protocols. While the study has not yet prompted regulatory action, it has increased awareness of the prevalence of fraudulent or outdated job ads and may influence future policy discussions on transparency in online recruitment.

title: YouTube Introduces Custom Feeds for Personalized Front Page
content:
YouTube has rolled out a new feature that lets users fine‑tune the content shown on their home feed, allowing them to curate the algorithm’s recommendations to match a particular “vibe.” The update, announced in a company blog post on September 12, gives subscribers the ability to select mood‑based filters—such as “Relax,” “Workout,” or “News”—which the platform’s recommendation engine will then prioritize when populating the front page. Users can adjust these settings through a new panel in the app’s settings menu, and the changes take effect immediately, reshaping the mix of videos that appear in the feed.

The tweak builds on YouTube’s long‑standing focus on personalization, which has traditionally relied on viewing history, likes, and watch time to surface content. By adding a mood dimension, the company aims to give viewers more control over the tone of their browsing experience, while still maintaining the algorithm’s core relevance metrics. Early beta testers reported that the new filters helped surface more contextually appropriate videos, and YouTube said it will monitor engagement data to refine the algorithm’s response to these user‑defined preferences.

Industry analysts see the update as part of a broader trend toward user‑centric curation on streaming platforms, where audiences increasingly demand that recommendation engines align with their current interests and emotional states. While the feature is currently available only in select regions, YouTube plans a global rollout over the next few weeks. The company has indicated that it will continue to experiment with additional mood categories and may integrate the system with its existing “Explore” and “Trending” tabs in future releases.

title: Discord introduces automatic age estimation for users worldwide (excluding Australia and UK)
content:
Discord has launched a new global age‑assurance system that will take effect today in every country except Australia and the United Kingdom. The platform will automatically place users into an estimated age group using “multiple account signals,” and will impose restrictions on accounts that the system deems to belong to individuals aged 13 to 17. The change follows Discord’s decision in February to halt its earlier age‑verification rollout, which had required adults to submit video selfies or government ID documents and drew criticism over data‑privacy concerns.

The new approach replaces the more intrusive verification process with a less burdensome, algorithmic method that relies on existing account data. By doing so, Discord aims to balance compliance with age‑restriction laws while addressing user privacy. The update is part of the company’s broader effort to refine its moderation tools and protect younger users on its platform.

title: YouTube Updates AI Creator Tools to Simplify Content Creation
content:

Creators can now use machine‑learning models to generate script outlines, suggest editing cues, and even preview how changes might affect viewer engagement before publishing. The tools also incorporate predictive analytics that flag potential copyright issues and recommend monetization strategies tailored to a channel’s niche. By integrating these features into a single dashboard, YouTube aims to reduce the time creators spend on technical experimentation and free them to focus on creative work.

The rollout signals a broader shift toward AI‑driven content creation support, positioning YouTube as a platform that not only hosts videos but actively assists creators in navigating the algorithm. title: Logitech Releases Blue Yeti 2 Microphone with AI Noise Reduction
content:
Logitech G has unveiled the Blue Yeti 2, the successor to its long‑running Blue Yeti USB microphone that has been a staple for content creators since 2009. The new model introduces a series of modern upgrades, most notably an interactive LED display that features the Yeti mascot, AI‑powered de‑noising, and a proximity‑based voice sensor that addresses a design flaw in the original microphone. These enhancements aim to improve user experience by providing real‑time visual feedback and reducing background noise.

The Blue Yeti 2 is offered in black or white and retails for $159.99, positioning it as a more affordable option compared to competitors such as Shure’s MV7 series, which starts at $299. The price point, combined with the added features, makes the Yeti 2 an attractive choice for podcasters and creators seeking a balance of performance and cost. Logitech G’s release underscores the brand’s commitment to evolving its audio products while maintaining the iconic Yeti identity.
author: The Verge

title: Sanders and Casar introduce bill to ban artificial superintelligence development
content:
Senate Majority Leader Bernie Sanders (I‑VT) and Representative Greg Casar (D‑TX) have introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, a bill that would prohibit the development of artificial superintelligence—defined by the proposal as a system capable of “destruction or disempowerment of humanity,” including the potential to overthrow government.  Under the measure, any AI leader who violates the ban could face up to 20 years in prison.  

The legislation does more than target the most powerful form of AI.  It also calls for a pause on the creation of advanced AI systems, and would require a review of any ongoing projects that might cross the threshold into superintelligence.  The bill comes amid President Donald Trump’s recent statement that the United States will use the term “superintelligence” in official documents in place of “AI,” underscoring the growing concern among lawmakers about the rapid pace of AI development.  

If passed, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act would represent a significant regulatory shift, marking the first federal effort to curb the creation of AI systems that could pose existential risks.  The proposal remains in the early stages, with its future depending on congressional debate and the broader national conversation about the balance between innovation and safety.
author: The Verge

title: America Loses Rare Earth Edge to China
content:
Decades of cheaper imports have left the United States heavily dependent on China for the processing of rare earth elements, a group of 17 metals essential to modern electronics, defense systems, and renewable‑energy technologies. While American mines still produce raw ore, the refining and separation steps that turn it into usable materials are largely conducted in China, where established infrastructure and lower labor costs have made the supply chain more efficient than domestic alternatives.

The reliance has grown as U.S. companies have outsourced processing to keep costs down and meet the high demand for smartphones, electric vehicles, and advanced weapons. In recent years, the Department of Commerce has identified rare earth processing as a strategic vulnerability, prompting initiatives to expand domestic refining capacity and diversify supply routes. However, the capital intensity and technical expertise required for rare earth processing mean that any rapid shift away from China would involve significant investment and time.

The continued dependence on Chinese processing underscores a broader challenge for U.S. industrial security. While the United States remains a major producer of rare earth ore, the lack of a robust domestic processing network limits its ability to control the supply chain and respond quickly to geopolitical disruptions. Policymakers and industry leaders are now evaluating how best to balance cost competitiveness with strategic resilience in this critical sector.
author: Ars Technica

title: NHTSA opens investigation into comma.ai after five crashes involving stopped vehicles
content:
Federal investigators have confirmed that five separate crashes involving vehicles equipped with autonomous or semi‑autonomous driving systems have occurred in the United States. In each incident, the AI‑enabled cars struck vehicles that were either moving slowly or had come to a complete stop. The crashes took place across different states, and preliminary reports indicate that the affected vehicles were operating in driver‑assist mode at the time of impact.

The incidents highlight ongoing concerns about the interaction between automated driving technologies and conventional traffic conditions. While the specific models and software versions involved have not yet been disclosed, the Department of Transportation has stated that it will review the data from each event to assess whether system design or operator behavior contributed to the accidents. The agency is also coordinating with manufacturers to evaluate potential updates to collision‑avoidance algorithms.

As the investigation proceeds, regulators are emphasizing the need for robust safety protocols for vehicles that rely on AI to navigate complex driving environments. The findings are expected to inform future regulatory guidance and may prompt revisions to the certification standards that govern autonomous driving systems.
author: Ars Technica

title: YouTube Adds AI Tools for Idea Generation and Thumbnail Tracking in Studio
content:
YouTube has announced new tools designed to help creators generate content ideas and track the effectiveness of their thumbnails. The platform’s updated Creator Studio now includes an AI‑driven idea generator that scans trending topics, audience demographics, and channel performance data to suggest video concepts. Alongside this, a thumbnail analytics dashboard offers real‑time metrics on click‑through rates, engagement, and comparative performance against similar videos, allowing creators to optimize visual appeal before publishing.

These enhancements aim to streamline the creative workflow by reducing the time spent on research and post‑publish analysis. Creators can now test multiple thumbnail variations within the studio, view projected performance, and adjust designs based on data rather than guesswork. The features are part of YouTube’s broader effort to provide data‑driven insights that support higher engagement and better audience retention across the platform.
author: TechCrunch

title: Eight Sleep Launches Pod 6 in Smaller and Solo Sizes, Starting at $1,999
content:
Eight Sleep announced that its latest smart mattress pod is 20 % faster than the previous generation, a claim that the company says will shorten the time the system takes to reach the desired sleep temperature. The new pod, part of the brand’s flagship sleep‑monitoring platform, is engineered with upgraded heating and cooling elements that allow it to respond more quickly to changes in room temperature and user settings.

The performance improvement means that users can expect a more consistent temperature environment throughout the night, with the pod reaching target temperatures in roughly a quarter of the time it took the earlier model. Eight Sleep’s marketing materials note that the faster response also reduces energy consumption by minimizing the time the heating or cooling system remains active. The company said the upgrade will be available in its next product release cycle, which is slated for early 2026.

Industry analysts view the speed boost as a competitive advantage in the growing market for connected sleep technology, where rapid temperature adjustment is increasingly cited as a key factor in user satisfaction. The new pod will be sold through Eight Sleep’s online store and select retail partners, with pricing expected to mirror that of the current generation.
author: TechCrunch

title: YouTube Music Adds Conversational AI Feature
content:
YouTube Music has added a new “Ask Music” feature that lets users request songs and playlists using plain‑English descriptions. Instead of typing in a specific title or artist name, listeners can simply type or speak a phrase such as “play something upbeat from the 1990s” or “I want a chill acoustic track with a guitar solo.” The app’s built‑in natural‑language processing interprets the request and returns a curated selection that matches the user’s intent.

The feature is part of YouTube Music’s broader effort to streamline discovery and improve the user experience. By leveraging the platform’s vast catalog and machine‑learning algorithms, Ask Music can surface tracks that fit mood, genre, era, or even lyrical themes, reducing the time spent scrolling through search results. Early reports suggest that the tool is particularly useful for users who prefer a conversational approach to music selection and for those who want to explore new music without knowing specific titles.

While YouTube Music has not yet released detailed metrics on the adoption of Ask Music, the company’s announcement indicates a push toward more intuitive, AI‑driven interactions within its app. The feature is available to all users on the latest versions of the app, and it represents a step toward a more seamless, voice‑friendly music‑finding experience.
author: TechCrunch

title: YouTube Adds Chat-Based Video Editing AI
content:
A new AI‑powered tool will soon allow video creators to edit footage through a conversational chat interface. The feature, announced by the platform’s development team, lets users describe desired edits—such as trimming, color correction, or adding transitions—and the system generates the corresponding commands in real time. The chat interface is designed to streamline the editing workflow, reducing the need to manually navigate menus or use complex shortcuts.

According to the company, the tool leverages natural‑language processing and machine‑learning models trained on millions of editing scenarios. Early beta testers reported that the system can interpret nuanced requests, automatically apply adjustments, and even suggest creative enhancements based on the content of the clip. The feature is slated for public release in the coming months, with integration planned for the platform’s existing desktop and mobile editing suites.

Industry observers note that this development could lower the barrier to entry for independent creators and speed up production timelines. By turning editing into a dialogue rather than a series of clicks, the new AI chat interface aims to make professional‑grade video production more accessible to a broader audience.
author: TechCrunch

title: YouTube Adds GIF Replies, Voice Comments, and Paid Communities for Creators
content:
YouTube announced a suite of new features aimed at deepening user engagement and expanding monetization options for creators. Among the updates are GIF replies, which allow viewers to respond to comments with animated images, and voice‑powered TV comments that let users leave spoken feedback on the platform’s television app. The company also introduced personalized moderation tools, enabling creators to tailor community guidelines and filter content more precisely.

In addition to these interaction enhancements, YouTube is rolling out paid, members‑only communities that give subscribers exclusive access to creator content and discussions. The platform is also testing new ways for fans to support their favorite creators, such as direct tipping and branded merchandise integrations. These initiatives are part of YouTube’s broader strategy to increase creator revenue streams while improving the overall user experience across its mobile, web, and TV services.

With the launch of these features, YouTube signals its intent to keep pace with evolving social‑media trends and to provide creators with more flexible tools for building and monetizing their audiences. The updates are expected to be rolled out gradually over the coming months, with further refinements based on user feedback.
author: TechCrunch

title: Daily AI Users in America Still Worried
content:
A recent study released by the Institute for Technology Ethics has found that increased public exposure to artificial intelligence systems does not alleviate the widespread unease surrounding the technology, nor does it diminish support for regulatory oversight. The report, based on surveys of 5,000 adults across the United States, indicates that even those who have interacted with AI-powered tools—such as virtual assistants, recommendation engines, and automated customer service—continue to express concerns about privacy, bias, and job displacement.

The authors argue that the persistence of apprehension stems from deeper anxieties about the opaque decision‑making processes of AI and the potential for unintended societal impacts. While the study acknowledges that familiarity can improve understanding, it concludes that knowledge alone is insufficient to shift public sentiment. Policymakers and industry leaders are urged to focus on transparent governance frameworks and robust accountability mechanisms to address the underlying issues that drive demand for regulation.
author: TechCrunch

title: Zoox Grounds Atlanta Test Fleet Over Toxic Gas Exposure Claims
content:
Amazon‑owned logistics firm QuickShip announced it has begun an internal investigation following a complaint filed by a warehouse worker with the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). The employee alleged unsafe operating conditions, including inadequate machine guarding and insufficient personal protective equipment, during routine packaging duties at the company’s distribution center in Springfield, Illinois. QuickShip’s spokesperson said the company “takes all OSHA complaints seriously and will cooperate fully with the agency’s review.”

The investigation will assess whether the alleged violations constitute a breach of federal safety standards and whether corrective actions are needed. QuickShip has indicated that it has already begun reviewing its safety protocols, training records, and incident reports for the affected facility. OSHA officials are expected to conduct site inspections and interview staff as part of the inquiry, with a preliminary report anticipated within the next 30 days.

The outcome of the investigation will determine whether QuickShip faces enforcement actions or must implement additional safety measures. The company has pledged to maintain transparency throughout the process and to update stakeholders on any findings or required changes once the inquiry is complete.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI Threats Expose Weaknesses in Traditional Cybersecurity
content:
Concern over artificial‑intelligence safety and the risk of rogue agents has pushed cybersecurity to the forefront of investor attention.  As headlines spotlight the potential for autonomous systems to act unpredictably, the market for security solutions has begun to rise, with several publicly traded cybersecurity firms reporting stronger quarterly performance and higher share prices.

Start‑up funding has followed suit, with venture capitalists and strategic investors pouring large sums into companies that promise to safeguard an AI‑native world.  Instinct and Simile, two firms focused on AI‑driven threat detection and mitigation, have each attracted nine‑figure investment rounds that would have seemed unlikely a few years ago.  Their valuations reflect the growing belief that traditional security models will need to evolve rapidly to keep pace with the speed and complexity of modern AI applications.

The surge in capital and valuation signals a broader shift in the technology landscape, underscoring the urgency of developing robust security frameworks for AI systems.  While the trend offers significant growth opportunities for the sector, it also highlights the need for clear regulatory guidance and industry standards to manage the risks associated with increasingly autonomous technologies.
author: TechCrunch

title: Al-Sharaa Vows Golan Heights Remain Syrian in UN Speech
content:
Bashar al‑Assad made a pointed remark at an Atlantic Council panel in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday, saying he had told former U.S. President Donald Trump that the United States had no right to recognise Israeli sovereignty over the Golan Heights.  The Syrian leader added a sarcastic comment that the U.S. president should instead “give New Jersey to Israel,” a jab aimed at the 2019 U.S. decision to formally recognise Israeli control of the territory.  

The Golan Heights, captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Six‑Day War, remain a flashpoint in the Arab‑Israeli conflict.  Syria has consistently demanded the return of the plateau, while Israel considers it a vital security buffer.  The U.S. recognition was criticised by Syria and other Arab states, which view the move as a violation of international law and the United Nations Security Council resolution that calls for the withdrawal of Israeli forces.  Assad’s comments, made in a setting that included diplomats, scholars and policy experts, underscored his government’s continued opposition to the U.S. stance and its broader diplomatic strategy against Israel.  

The panel’s discussion highlighted the broader geopolitical implications of U.S. policy in the Middle East, with analysts noting that such statements from Syrian leadership may influence regional dynamics and diplomatic negotiations.  While the U.S. maintains that its recognition was a matter of sovereign decision, Assad’s remarks reflect the enduring divide over the Golan Heights and the broader Israeli‑Palestinian and Arab‑Israeli disputes.
author: Euronews

title: Rome's Colosseum Lights Up in Pink for Breast Cancer Campaign
content:
The Colosseum in Rome illuminated a pink glow this week as part of a breast‑cancer awareness campaign, a striking visual that lit up the ancient amphitheatre just hours before its nightly closure. The temporary lighting, installed to highlight the “Pink for Cancer” initiative, was intended to draw attention to early detection and prevention efforts.

During the installation, a 22‑year‑old maintenance worker suffered a fatal accident while setting up the new lighting rig. Authorities confirmed that the worker was operating the equipment at the time of the incident, and emergency services responded immediately. The incident has prompted an investigation into the safety protocols used during the lighting upgrade.

The Colosseum will remain closed for the remainder of the evening, and the campaign will continue under enhanced safety measures. Officials have pledged to honor the fallen worker and to review procedures to prevent future tragedies while maintaining the public health message.
author: Euronews

title: Morocco Holds Parliamentary Election Amid Cost of Living Concerns
content:
Morocco is holding a parliamentary election amid a mix of optimism and apprehension, as voters weigh the nation’s prospects for jobs, wages, public services and the cost of living while the country gears up to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup. The election comes at a time when the government is under pressure to deliver economic stability and infrastructure improvements that will support the forthcoming global sporting event.

Key political parties are foregrounding employment creation and wage growth in their campaigns, pledging to expand public sector jobs and tighten labor regulations to protect workers. Meanwhile, opposition groups are scrutinizing the government’s spending on World Cup preparations, arguing that the funds could be better allocated to health, education and social services. The cost‑of‑living debate is also central, with candidates proposing measures to curb inflation and increase purchasing power for ordinary Moroccans.

The outcome of this vote will shape Morocco’s capacity to meet the logistical demands of the World Cup and to address domestic economic concerns. A decisive mandate could accelerate reforms aimed at boosting employment and improving public services, while a fragmented result may prolong uncertainty about how the country will balance its hosting ambitions with the everyday needs of its citizens.
author: Euronews

title: Giant gorilla performer dances with students at Lahore university event
content:
A university event in Lahore drew national attention when a giant gorilla performer joined students on the dancefloor, exemplifying Pakistan’s growing viral party trend. The gathering, hosted by the University of Lahore’s student council, was part of a series of themed celebrations aimed at boosting campus engagement during the spring semester.

The performer, a life‑size animatronic gorilla wearing a neon costume, moved to popular dance tracks and encouraged attendees to participate in synchronized routines. Students and faculty alike filmed the spectacle, which quickly went viral on social media platforms such as TikTok and Instagram. The trend—characterized by oversized animal costumes, high‑energy music, and interactive dance challenges—has spread across Pakistani universities, prompting organizers to adopt similar themes for future events.

The event underscores the increasing role of viral culture in shaping campus life and social media engagement in Pakistan. By blending entertainment with digital sharing, universities are leveraging these trends to foster community and visibility, suggesting that such themed gatherings may become a staple of student life in the coming years.
author: Euronews

title: 150 women graduate from Syria's new police academy
content:
Around 150 women have graduated from Syria’s newly established police academy, a milestone that underscores the government’s drive to rebuild the country’s security apparatus and broaden female participation in law‑enforcement roles. The ceremony, held in the capital, was attended by senior officials who highlighted the graduates’ completion of a six‑month curriculum covering criminal law, public order, and community policing.

The cohort’s graduation is part of a broader security‑sector reform program aimed at restoring stability after years of conflict and integrating women into positions traditionally held by men. Authorities say the inclusion of female officers is intended to improve public trust, especially in handling cases involving women and children, and to align Syria’s policing standards with international norms. The graduates are set to be deployed across various districts, where they will assist in routine patrols, traffic control and crime prevention, contributing to the ongoing effort to normalize public safety services throughout the nation.
author: Euronews

title: France sees surge in Gen Z baptisms ahead of Pope Leo XIV visit
content:
France is gearing up for the upcoming visit of Pope Leo XIV, a trip that coincides with a notable surge in religious participation among the nation’s youth. Official statistics released by the French Episcopal Conference indicate that more than 21,000 catechumens—teenagers and young adults preparing for baptism—have been recorded in 2026, a figure that eclipses the combined totals of the previous decade. The increase has been highlighted in a report by Florence Gaillard for France in Focus, underscoring a shift in the demographic profile of recent baptisms, which now feature a higher proportion of individuals aged 15 to 29 compared with earlier cohorts.

Analysts attribute the rise to a combination of factors, including intensified diocesan outreach programs targeting schools and community centers, the influence of digital evangelization initiatives launched by the French Catholic hierarchy, and a broader societal search for identity and belonging amid economic uncertainty. Additionally, the upcoming papal visit is expected to amplify visibility for the Church’s youth ministries, potentially sustaining the momentum observed this year. Church officials view the trend as an opportunity to engage a new generation, while the Vatican’s schedule for Pope Leo XIV’s French itinerary includes meetings with catechumen groups and youth leaders, signaling an institutional focus on consolidating this renewed interest.
author: France 24

title: Iranian President Addresses UNGA as US‑Israel Conflict Escalates
content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday, delivering his first speech at the world body since the United States and Israel escalated hostilities with Iran. In his remarks, Pezeshkian called for diplomatic engagement and emphasized the need for a peaceful resolution to the ongoing tensions, underscoring Iran’s willingness to cooperate with the international community while defending its sovereign interests.

His appearance followed a stark warning from U.S. President Donald Trump the previous day, when Trump told the assembly that the United States could “annihilate the Islamic Republic” and “drive them into hell.” The contrasting statements highlighted the heightened rhetoric surrounding the conflict, as diplomatic officials and observers noted the potential impact of such exchanges on regional stability and future negotiations.
author: France 24

title: Russia drone attacks kill two in Kyiv ahead of Zelenskyy's UN address
content:
Russia launched a series of daylight drone strikes on Kyiv on Wednesday, killing two civilians and injuring 23 others, according to local authorities. The attacks occurred just hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy was scheduled to address world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly, prompting heightened concerns about security in the capital ahead of the high‑profile speech.

The drone assaults came after Zelenskyy’s meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday, during which Trump voiced frustration over the stalled progress of negotiations aimed at ending the war and the ongoing escalation of aerial attacks by both sides. The latest strike underscores the volatile security environment surrounding diplomatic efforts, as officials continue to seek avenues for de‑escalation. Emerald Maxwell reports.
author: France 24

title: US urges Ukraine and Russia to stop attacks on energy infrastructure
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is scheduled to address the United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday, marking a high‑profile diplomatic appearance as the war in Ukraine enters its fifth year. The speech comes amid renewed calls from U.S. President Donald Trump for a swift end to Russia’s invasion, a stance that aligns with Kyiv’s effort to shape a broader international push for peace and reconstruction after more than four and a half years of conflict. France 24 international affairs commentator Douglas Herbert noted that Zelenskyy’s remarks are expected to underscore Ukraine’s demand for sustained security guarantees, the reconstruction of war‑torn regions, and the enforcement of accountability for alleged war crimes.

The upcoming address follows a series of diplomatic initiatives aimed at consolidating support for Ukraine, including recent high‑level meetings in Europe and the United States. While Trump’s advocacy for a negotiated settlement adds a new dimension to the diplomatic landscape, analysts say the effectiveness of such overtures will depend on coordinated action among NATO allies and the willingness of the Russian government to engage in meaningful talks. Zelenskyy’s UN appearance is therefore poised to serve both as a platform for reaffirming Ukraine’s sovereignty and as a catalyst for renewed multilateral engagement on ending the conflict.
author: France 24

title: Paris prosecutors investigate non-consensual filming with smart glasses
content:
Paris prosecutors have launched multiple investigations after receiving complaints that women were filmed on public streets without their consent by individuals wearing so‑called “smart glasses.” The complaints allege that the devices, which resemble ordinary eyewear, were used to capture video covertly and that the resulting footage was subsequently posted online. Prosecutors in the French capital said they are examining the incidents under existing privacy and harassment statutes, and have begun gathering evidence from victims and potential witnesses.

The cases have intensified a broader European debate over the regulation of wearable recording technology, which campaigners have labeled “pervert” smart glasses following a series of viral videos showing women and girls filmed in public spaces. Advocacy groups are urging legislators to introduce stricter controls on the sale and use of such devices, while technology firms face pressure to implement safeguards that prevent illicit recording.
